newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS says new provisions may be higher in H2.
newsitem.headline: UBS says new provisions may be higher in H2.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said it may take higher new provisions for credit risk in the second of 1997 than in the first six months, when it set aside 137 million Swiss francs for new credit and country risks.
UBS also said it had used roughly 800 million Swiss francs in the first half of 1997 from an exceptional charge of three billion francs that it took last year to cover weak Swiss loans.

This meant there were still about 2.2 billion Swiss francs available in the one-time provision, which the bank set aside last year to end mounting problems among Swiss loans hit by a stubbornly slow economy.
UBS said its decision to take the three-billion charge last year was an important reason for a strong 67.4 percent rise in net profit in the first half of 1997 to 1,856 million swiss francs.
The first-half level of new credit and country risk provisions of 137 million francs was down 82 percent from 776 million a year earlier, UBS said.
"Our provisioning requirements are likely to be higher in the second half of the year, however," it said in a letter to shareholders.
"This is because new provisions charged to earnings in the first half of the year were below statistical projections."

"Although the latest economic data coming in are somewhat more encouraging, for Switzerland as well, no immediate positive impact can be expected on the loan portfolio," the letter added without elaborating further.
